title: Each other
goal: Talk about what people do to each other: tanışmak, anlaşmak, barışmak, birbirimizi.

intro.text: `-(I)ş` makes a verb for what people do to each other: *tanışmak* (to meet), *buluşmak* (to meet up), *anlaşmak* (to get along). For other verbs, use *birbiri* with a possessive: *Birbirimizi seviyoruz* (We love each other).

vocab.en: to make up, to make peace
to leave; to split up, to break up
each other (birbirimizi: each other, for we)
to text each other, to message each other

exercises.en: Ayşe and I met at a wedding.

reject.why: *Tanıdık* is **we knew, we recognized**. **To meet, to get to know each other** is the reciprocal: *tanı-ş-tı-k*.

exercises.explain: *tanı-* ends in a vowel, so the reciprocal is just *-ş*; the past after ş is *-tı*: *tanı-ş-tı-k*.

exercises.question: Which sentence means **We love each other**?

exercises.label: *anlaşmak*, present continuous: I get along (with someone), you get along…
exercises.explain: *anla-ş-* is a new stem; `-(I)yor` and the endings follow: *anla-ş-ıyor-um*.

exercises.prompt: I made up with my brother.

reject.why: *Barışmak* takes no object: the other person comes with *ile*: *kardeşimle*.

exercises.en: We've known each other for years.

exercises.prompt: Çocuklar kavga etti ama hemen barıştılar.
accept: The children had a fight but made up right away.
The children [fought|argued|quarrelled|quarreled|had an argument] but (they) made up [right away|immediately|at once|straight away].
The children had a fight but (they) made up [immediately|at once|straight away].
The children had a fight but they made up right away.
The kids [fought|had a fight|argued|had an argument] but (they) made up [right away|immediately|at once|straight away].

exercises.prompt: Shall we meet in front of the cinema at seven?
exercises.text: Saat yedide sinemanın önünde buluşalım mı?
accept: Sinemanın önünde saat yedide buluşalım mı?

exercises.text: Kardeşimle çok iyi ___ ama bazen tartışıyoruz.
exercises.en: My brother and I get along very well, but sometimes we argue.
exercises.explain: *Kardeşimle … anlaşıyoruz*: with *-le*, the **we** ending means **my brother and I**. *Anlıyoruz* is **we understand**, *anlatıyoruz* **we tell**.

exercises.question: What happened between Deniz and Emre?

context.tr: Hayır, geçen ay ayrıldık. Ama hâlâ arkadaşız.
context.en: No, we split up last month. But we're still friends.

options: They split up but stayed friends
They had a fight and stopped speaking
exercises.explain: *Ayrıldık*, with a **we** ending: the two of them **split up**. *Görüşmek* here is **to see each other**.

exercises.prompt: Ali ile Ayşe birbirlerine çok benziyor.
accept: Ali and Ayşe look very much alike.
Ali and Ayşe [look like|resemble] each other a lot.
Ali and Ayşe [really|very much] [look like|resemble] each other.
Ali and Ayşe look a lot like each other.

exercises.en: We hugged each other at the airport.

reject.why: *Birbirimize* is **each other** for **we**, so the verb takes *-k*: *sarıldık*.

exercises.explain: *Sarılmak* takes the dative: *birbirimize sarıldık*, **we hugged each other**.
